absent: Threaded disable work and exit propagation work behavior beyond queueing.
Dispatch queue implementation, bypass handling and load-balancing timer actions.
Arena pool, kernel objects, capability and shard initialization details.
Task iterator contract, scheduler class selection and slice management.
Sysfs attributes, uevents and kobject release path beyond insertion.
Watchdog enforcement, stall tracking and diagnostic dump contents.
Bandwidth reservation accounting for server entities.

findings.text: Exposes a blocking quiescence helper for scheduler teardown that callers invoke to wait until disable-related interrupt and thread work have drained.
Exposes a constructor that builds a scheduler instance from an enable command with optional parent linkage, reporting resource exhaustion through an encoded error pointer.
Exposes a publication helper that inserts an initialized scheduler object into the scheduler sysfs hierarchy with separate placement for top level and nested instances.
Exposes a validation helper that rejects incompatible operation flag combinations and mismatched operation table forms.
Exposes a helper that moves a task into first-in-first-out real-time policy at a mid-range priority.
Quiescence is defined by the exit progress marker reaching either idle or fully completed; any other marker causes synchronization to repeat.
Exit notification arriving in hard interrupt context triggers conditional diagnostic capture for severe exits and always delegates further teardown to a helper thread.

Kick coordination state exists as one table per possible processor, each table holding one entry per processor in the system, allocated local to the owning node and fully released if any processor fails.
Per-node container couples allocation with initialization of its node-wide shared queue; queue failure implies container release and a null result.
Unspecified dispatch batch size, watchdog interval and base time slice fall back to built-in defaults, and the exit marker starts idle.

Visibility to concurrent readers begins when the instance is linked from the operations private area; earlier failures unwind locally while later failures rely on deferred reference-counted reclamation.

Root bring-up serializes concurrent enable attempts with a dedicated mutex, stabilizes processor set membership during critical construction, and excludes task creation plus cgroup membership changes while existing tasks are prepared.
Bandwidth reservation changes for server entities occur with the run-queue lock held and the queue clock refreshed, applied independently per possible processor.

Scheduler instance aggregates exit diagnostics, dispatch hash, per-node pointers, per-processor area, helper thread, ancestry chain with depth and identity, timing knobs, exit synchronization primitives, load-balancing masks and timer, operation table views, cgroup linkage and kernel object membership.
Per-processor scheduler area links back to its instance and carries deferred local work lists plus separate processor sets for wake, conditional wake, preemption and waiting.
Per-node scheduler area centers on a node-wide shared dispatch queue bound to its owning instance.
Global enable progresses from disabled through an enabling intermediate to enabled, with single-flight guards and rollback to disabled or diversion into the disable path on failure.
Per-task attachment moves from uninitialized through begin and intermediate stages to ready, with a distinct dead marker allowing safe rendezvous when teardown races initialization.
Exit progress distinguishes idle start, in-progress teardown, completed teardown and a severity threshold at or above which diagnostics are captured.
Workqueue handler serving as the root attach entry point, consuming an enable command and producing a success or failure status for the waiter.
Hard interrupt work handler serving as the asynchronous exit notification entry point for a scheduler instance.

Enable aborts when processor topology changed since scheduler initialization, when a prior instance teardown is still publishing, when any task preparation fails, or when bandwidth reservation cannot be satisfied.
Two operation table forms coexist with different lengths; nested scheduling and associated attach interfaces require the shorter form, while reading trailing members from that form would overrun.
Lifecycle markers distinguish idle, done and error severity, and dispatch queue identities distinguish node-global and per-processor bypass channels.
Operation flags control last-enqueue semantics, task lookup by identifier, built-in idle selection variants, partial versus full switching and recorded preemption support.
Resource, busy and argument failures are reported with standard negative codes, and helper promotion uses FIFO policy at half the maximum real-time priority.
